name: awesome-flight-data
what_it_holds: A curated 'awesome list' cataloguing flight-data APIs and providers across categories: seat maps/booking (Duffel, Sabre), schedules/seats/capacity (OAG Flight Info API, Cirium Developer Studio), ADS-B/tracking (Flightradar24 API, OpenSky Network API, FlightAware AeroAPI), and historical schedules (Aviation Edge, aviationstack, AeroDataBox, FlightLabs, AirLabs). No data itself, just a map of where to look, including the one named source in our theme (aviationstack) and the closest thing to a paid seat-capacity API (OAG).
why_useful: Confirms that true public/free airline seat-capacity-by-route data does not exist on GitHub as a committed dataset -- the closest real feeds (OAG, Cirium) are paid APIs, which narrows this theme's actionable candidates to BTS T-100 (via skynet) and OpenSky-derived flight counts as the realistic free substitutes.
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: Confirms that true public/free airline seat-capacity-by-route data does not exist on GitHub as a committed dataset -- the closest real feeds (OAG, Cirium) are paid APIs, which narrows this theme's actionable candidates to BTS T-100 (via skynet) and OpenSky-derived flight counts as the realistic free substitutes.

name: pruatlas
what_it_holds: R package of EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit airspace GIS layers (FIR/ANSP boundaries) and mapping helpers, based on a single 2015 AIRAC snapshot. Confirmed via WebFetch: NOT a traffic-volume or passenger-count dataset, just cartography for PRU publications.
why_useful: Pure airspace geography/mapping utility, no passenger or traffic volume figures; only useful as a plotting aid if building airspace maps, not a KPI input.
themes: European and global aviation stats: Eurocontrol, EASA, ACI airport passenger stats, IATA public figures, airport monthly traffic scrapers (Heathrow, Schiphol, ADP, Fraport, AENA)

why_all: Pure airspace geography/mapping utility, no passenger or traffic volume figures; only useful as a plotting aid if building airspace maps, not a KPI input.

Flagging as a dead end for idea #8 (bilateral air-passenger traffic): this is the closest EUROCONTROL-adjacent open repo found and it does not hold what we need. A real Eurocontrol/IATA passenger-volume-by-route open dataset was not located on GitHub in this pass.

name: Montecarlo-GBM-Analysis (Jordan Tourism Board passenger demand)
what_it_holds: Passenger-demand forecasting project for the Jordan Tourism Board using OAG Traffic Analyser data (2012-2025), World Bank WDI, UNWTO, and IMF WEO series; OLS log-log regression, residual-based Monte Carlo and GBM simulation; forecast horizon 2025-2030 (6 years forward, 13 years historical).
why_useful: Not a data source for our specific countries, but a worked methods example (log-log demand regression + GBM Monte Carlo on air-traffic + UNWTO + WDI inputs) that is directly transferable to nowcasting/forecasting international arrivals as a leading indicator for ABNB APAC/LatAm nights -- fits the 'methods_tooling' gap (#17, mixed-frequency/demand-forecasting methods).
themes: International arrivals: NTTO I-94, UNWTO, StatCan travellers, JNTO Japan, Korea KTO, Australia ABS overseas arrivals, Mexico INEGI/DATATUR, Brazil, Thailand MOTS, Indonesia BPS, India MoT
Tourism satellite accounts and tourism spending data: WTTC, UNWTO, BEA travel and tourism satellite account, national tourism expenditure surveys
why_all: Not a data source for our specific countries, but a worked methods example (log-log demand regression + GBM Monte Carlo on air-traffic + UNWTO + WDI inputs) that is directly transferable to nowcasting/forecasting international arrivals as a leading indicator for ABNB APAC/LatAm nights -- fits the 'methods_tooling' gap (#17, mixed-frequency/demand-forecasting methods).

A worked example combining airline traffic (OAG) with UNWTO/World Bank/IMF macro series for tourism-demand forecasting — a usable methods template for MIDAS/nowcasting-style work (gap #17) even though the underlying OAG data itself is licensed and likely not redistributed in full.

name: bis-med-it/pysdmx
what_it_holds: Bank for International Settlements-maintained Python SDMX library (29 stars) for reading/writing SDMX data and metadata, used internally at BIS and by some central banks for statistical exchange.
why_useful: Another actively maintained (BIS-backed) SDMX client that could substitute for a hand-rolled Eurostat/ISTAT puller; institutional backing suggests longevity.

name: transport-site
what_it_holds: Elixir/Phoenix codebase for transport.data.gouv.fr, France's National Access Point for mobility data — aggregates GTFS/GTFS-RT feeds from ~356 French transit authorities (76.3% population coverage per the site) including regional and national rail/bus operators, with feed validation and proxying tools. The site itself (not this code repo) is the actual place to pull French SNCF-adjacent GTFS feeds.
why_useful: Points to a comprehensive French national transit-data catalog (potentially including SNCF TER/Intercités GTFS and FlixBus France feeds) that a scraper/analyst could query for schedule/capacity data; the GitHub repo itself is only the platform's code, not the data.
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
